title: Please Add Swipe Back Gesture
body: Google Keep is a great app, but it really lacks one essential feature for iOS in 2025: the swipe back gesture. It makes no sense that we still need to tap the tiny back arrow in the top-left corner to exit a note, especially when its sensitivity and precision are far from ideal. Almost every modern iOS app supports swipe back as a standard navigation method, and its absence here feels outdated and frustrating. Please, Google, bring this small but crucial improvement — it would make the app much more fluid and user-friendly.
author: This Rusty Nail

title: Simples, rápida e indispensável para notas
body:
A app Google Keep é excelente! É super prática para criar notas rápidas, listas e lembretes, tudo de forma organizada e acessível em qualquer dispositivo.

Adoro a simplicidade do design e a rapidez com que consigo anotar ideias sem perder tempo. A sincronização funciona na perfeição, o que é ótimo para ter as notas sempre à mão, seja no telemóvel ou no computador.

Para mim, tornou-se uma aplicação indispensável no dia a dia.

title: Powerful but very very cluttered (or clutter inducing)
body: I’d always give Instapaper the edge over this one because of it’s clean uncluttered minimalist design. We use these apps to try to give some order to our lives. With Google Keep I just feel that everything still is a mess, never feeling I can count on this app to find my stuff, never feeling this should be my Internet snippets repository. I really love how Instapaper let’s everything packed is standardized sized boxes as if every information around the Internet could suddenly become part of a minimalist “bookshelf” of knowledge. Google Keep just looks like a messy kitchen “don’t forget” board. Even the “Post It” app I’ve tried, which is supposed to be sort of a messy board, let’s you rearrange and group stuff freely. Google Keep it has still a long path to go through.
